mainTopic: Sealed barrels held by a כותי, and why חז"ל forbade the beer of גוים (חתנות vs. גילוי)
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with an earlier source allowing sealed barrels held by a כותי. רבי זירא answers by splitting city from road. רבי ירמיה rejects that answer and says the lenient source is about barrels among the winepresses, where the כותי fears being seen. A new topic then opens: why did חז"ל forbid the beer of גוים? One view says חתנות (social closeness) and the other says גילוי (uncovered liquid that a snake may have poisoned). The גמרא defends the גילוי reason against two challenges. Next come stories of אמוראים who drank גוים' beer away from their company, and of רב שמואל בר ביסנא, who refused even beer as a 'trace of a trace.' Finally, רב permits Aramean beer but not for his weak son חייא, and שמואל adds teachings about venom. The amud ends as רב יוסף begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא that requires recognizing the seal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that a barrel sent with a כותי or a גוי is allowed only if the owner recognizes his seal. This seems to clash with the earlier source that allowed sealed barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sends a barrel of wine with a כותי, or a barrel of fish brine or fish stew with a גוי: if he recognizes his seal and his way of closing it, it is allowed. If not, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge the earlier source that allowed sealed barrels held by a כותי. Here a sealed barrel is not automatically fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source treated a sealed barrel with a כותי as safe. This ברייתא adds a condition: the owner must recognize his own seal and closing. Without that, it is forbidden. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan; someone whose care with wine is in question
Fish brine
A fish-based stew or sauce, which often had wine mixed in
His seal
His way of closing (stopping up) the barrel

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is not a new ruling standing on its own. The גמרא is using it as a challenge against the earlier lenient source about sealed barrels.

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן בְּיַד כּוּתִי,
phrases.english: One who sends a barrel of wine in the hands of a Samaritan,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל צִיר וְשֶׁל מוּרְיָיס בְּיַד גּוֹי,
phrases.english: or a barrel of fish brine or of fish stew in the hands of a gentile,
if he recognizes his seal and his way of closing it, it is permitted;
phrases.notes: "His" means the sender's own seal. He can tell that nobody opened it on the way.

phrases.english: if not, it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן בְּיַד כּוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier source (before this section) that allowed sealed barrels held by a כותי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ruling that sealed barrels with a כותי are allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a sealed barrel were enough, recognizing the seal would not be needed. This ברייתא requires it, so the two sources contradict.

steps.title: רבי זירא splits city from road
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the sources talk about different places: one is in the city and the other is on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It is not difficult. Here it is in the city; there it is on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the contradiction. He says the two sources are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the city, the כותי is careful because people may see him, so sealed barrels are allowed. On the road nobody is watching, so the owner must recognize his own seal. That is why the ברייתא is strict.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the sources do not really clash
Here... there; each source applies to a different case
In the city
On the road

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: It is not difficult.
Here it is in the city; there it is on the road.
phrases.notes: The lenient source is about the city. The strict ברייתא, which asks to recognize the seal, is about the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן בָּעִיר, כָּאן בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to rule differently on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the city sealed barrels are fine. On the road the owner must recognize his seal.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: city barrels also came by road
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה objects that barrels in the city also traveled on the road to get there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה challenged this: Didn't these barrels in the city also come by the road?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי זירא's answer. The city/road split does not really work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any barrel now in the city was carried there along a road. So whatever worry exists on the road applies to city barrels too. That means the city cannot be a safe case.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (attacked the previous answer)
Isn't it so that...? (a strong rhetorical question)
They came

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי הָנָךְ דְּעִיר לָא בְּדֶרֶךְ אָתוּ?
phrases.english: Didn't these barrels in the city come by the road?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's split between city and road
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: City barrels already passed through the road, so the road worry still applies to them.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the lenient source is about the winepresses
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the lenient source was taught about barrels among the winepresses. There everyone is around, so the כותי is afraid to let a גוי touch the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי ירמיה said: We learned it about barrels among the winepresses. Since everyone is around there, he is afraid. He says to himself: If they see me now, they will make me lose my business.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives his own answer to the contradiction from step 1. He limits the lenient source to the winepress area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the winepresses lots of people are always coming and going. The כותי worries that someone will catch him and Jews will stop buying from him. That fear keeps the sealed barrel safe there. Anywhere else, the strict ברייתא applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this drops the previous answer and gives a new one
Among the winepresses
He is afraid
They will make me lose (my business)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is רבי ירמיה's. A sealed barrel with a כותי is allowed only where he is afraid of being seen, like among the winepresses. Otherwise the owner must recognize his seal.
steps.whyThisMatters: The leniency is based on the כותי's fear of being caught. Where that fear exists, we can rely on him.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yirmeya says:
We learned it about barrels between the winepresses.
phrases.notes: "It" is the lenient source that allowed the sealed barrels.

phrases.english: Since everyone is around there, he is afraid,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: הַשְׁתָּא אִי חָזוּ לִי מַפְסְדוּ לִי.
phrases.english: as he says: Now, if they see me, they will make me lose my business.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: בֵּין הַגִּיתּוֹת שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי זירא's rejected answer with a new way to resolve the contradiction from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by a different factor: a busy winepress area vs. elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: City vs. road was the split, but it fell apart because city barrels also came by road.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient source is about the winepresses, where the כותי fears being seen and losing his Jewish customers.

steps.title: Why was the beer of גוים forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens: what was the reason חז"ל forbade beer made by גוים?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: For what reason did they forbid the beer of גוים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks for the reason behind the ban on beer of גוים and sets up the two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beer is not wine, so the usual wine worries do not explain the ban. The question is what other concern led חז"ל to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason?
Beer (an alcoholic drink, often made from dates or grain)

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָסְרוּ שֵׁכָר שֶׁל גּוֹיִם?
phrases.english: It was stated: For what reason did they prohibit the beer of gentiles?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָסְרוּ שֵׁכָר שֶׁל גּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the barrels discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind the ban on beer of גוים

steps.title: Two reasons: closeness or uncovered drink
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק (quoted by רמי בר חמא) says the reason is חתנות. רב נחמן says it is גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of רבי יצחק: because of intermarriage. רב נחמן said: because of being left uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, each with a different reason for the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's reason is social: drinking together brings closeness that can lead to marriage with גוים. רב נחמן's reason is safety: the beer may have been left uncovered. These two reasons can lead to different rules in different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Intermarriage; the worry that friendship over drinks leads to marrying גוים
Being left uncovered; the worry that a snake drank from it and left venom

steps.whyThisMatters: If the reason is חתנות, the worry is about drinking together. If it is גילוי, the worry is about the drink itself. The גמרא will build on this difference.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִשּׁוּם חַתְנוּת,
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama says that Rabbi Yitzḥak says: It is due to marriage.
phrases.notes: The worry is that drinking with גוים builds friendships that lead to marrying them.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: It is due to exposure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִשּׁוּם חַתְנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק: because of חתנות (social closeness leading to intermarriage). רב נחמן: because of גילוי (the drink may have been left uncovered).

steps.title: Which uncovered container is the worry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's reason of גילוי. Jews also leave vats and barrels uncovered, so why forbid only גוים' beer?
steps.simpleTranslation: Exposure of what? If you mean an uncovered vat, we also leave vats uncovered! And if you mean an uncovered barrel, we also leave barrels uncovered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's answer from Step 6. It asks what kind of uncovered beer he could mean, since Jews leave their beer uncovered the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reason for forbidding גוים' beer must point to something that is true only of גוים. The גמרא tries both possible containers, the brewing vat and the storage barrel. In both cases Jews do the same thing, so גילוי seems unable to explain a law aimed only at גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquid left uncovered, which might have been poisoned by a snake drinking from it
Vat, the large tub where the beer is brewed
Barrel, a storage container
If you say, used when testing one possible meaning

phrases.english: About exposure of what?
If you say exposure of the vat
we also leave it uncovered!
And rather, exposure of the barrel
we also leave it uncovered!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַגִּילּוּי דְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's reason (גילוי) from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reason that גוים' beer is forbidden because of גילוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every container where the beer might be left uncovered is left uncovered by Jews too. So גילוי cannot explain a law that applies only to beer made by גוים.

steps.title: The worry is water left standing to settle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the law is needed for a place where the water used for brewing is left standing to settle.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the law is needed for a place where they let the water settle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. The גילוי worry is not about the vat or the barrel. It is about the water, which is left standing to settle before brewing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry moves from the beer containers to an earlier stage, the water itself. In places where water is left standing to clear, it sits uncovered. That gives a real reason to suspect גוים' beer, which Jews' beer does not share.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for, used to narrow a ruling to a specific case
Place
They let the water settle and clear

phrases.english: No, it is needed
in a place where they let the water settle.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, בְּאַתְרָא דִּמְצַלּוּ מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the גילוי worry is about the water left to settle, not about the vat or barrel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: גילוי meant beer left uncovered in a vat or barrel, which Jews do too.
steps.terutzMaskana: גילוי refers to the water being left to settle, which gives a reason to suspect גוים' beer specifically.

steps.title: Then aged beer should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is גילוי, aged beer should be allowed. רבי teaches that a drink which aged or soured cannot have been poisoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, aged beer should be allowed! For רבי said: aged liquid is allowed, because poison would not let it age. Liquid that soured is allowed, because poison would not let it sour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. If poison is the only worry, then beer that has aged safely should be allowed, yet all גוים' beer is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי teaches that snake poison spoils a drink before it can age or sour. So aging proves the drink was never poisoned. Under the גילוי reason, aged beer should be completely fine.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, used to draw out a problem from what was just said
Aged, old
It turned sour

phrases.english: But if so, aged beer should be allowed!
For רבי said:
aged is allowed,
it does not let it age,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the snake's poison. A poisoned drink goes bad before it can grow old.

phrases.english: if it soured, it is allowed,
it does not let it sour.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה יָשָׁן תִּשְׁתְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of Step 8 but draws a new problem from the גילוי reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גילוי reason for forbidding גוים' beer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי teaches that aging proves a drink was never poisoned. So under the גילוי reason, aged beer should be allowed, but it is not.

steps.title: Aged beer is forbidden because of new beer
steps.stepSummary: חז"ל forbade aged beer too, so that people would not come to drink new beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a rabbinic decree: aged beer is forbidden because of new beer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that aged beer really is safe. חז"ל forbade it anyway so people would not confuse it with new beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law on aged beer is a fence, not a direct result of the danger. If aged beer were allowed, people might drink new beer, which could be poisoned. So the גילוי reason still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Because of, out of concern for
New

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's גילוי reason survives two challenges. The worry is water left to settle, and aged beer is forbidden only as a fence for new beer.

phrases.english: It is a decree: aged beer because of new beer.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה יָשָׁן אַטּוּ חָדָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic fence: the aged beer itself is safe, but it is forbidden as a safeguard.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under גילוי, aged beer should be allowed, since it cannot be poisoned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Aged beer is forbidden only as a decree, so people will not drink new beer.

steps.title: How רב פפא and רב אחאי drank גוים' beer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא drank גוים' beer at the store's doorway, and רב אחאי had it brought to his house. Both did this because of חתנות, but רב אחאי went beyond what was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא had the beer brought out to the doorway of the store, and he drank it. רב אחאי had it brought to his house, and he drank it. Both acted because of the worry of חתנות. רב אחאי was being extra careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how two אמוראים actually drank גוים' beer. Both kept away from socializing with the גוים, which follows the חתנות reason from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is חתנות (friendly drinking that leads to marriage), the beer itself is not the problem. The setting is the problem. So these אמוראים drank the beer away from the גוי's company. רב פפא's distance was enough, and רב אחאי added more than the law requires.

keyTerms.meaning: To the doorway of the store
Marriage ties, the worry that friendly drinking with גוים leads to intermarriage
Extra distancing, being stricter than required

phrases.english: For רב פפא, they would bring it out
to the doorway of the store, and he drank.
phrases.notes: Some versions spell the word one way, some the other. Either way it means 'to the doorway.'

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחַאי מַיְיתוּ לֵיהּ לְבֵיתֵיהּ, וְשָׁתֵי.
phrases.english: For רב אחאי, they would bring it to his house, and he drank.
And both of them acted because of marriage ties,
but רב אחאי made an extra distancing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא מַפְּיקִין לֵיהּ אַבָּבָא דְּחָנוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate over reasons to how אמוראים acted, based on the חתנות reason of Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the worry is חתנות, one may drink גוים' beer away from their social setting. Drinking at the store's doorway is enough, and taking it home is extra strictness.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר ביסנא refuses wine and beer
steps.stepSummary: In מרגואן, רב שמואל בר ביסנא was offered wine and then beer, and he drank neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר ביסנא came to מרגואן. They brought him wine and he did not drink it. They brought him beer and he did not drink it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about an אמורא who refused both wine and beer. It is setting up the question in the next step: why did he refuse the beer?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine refusal is explained in the next step by a שימצא, a trace or suspicion of idol-wine. Refusing the beer is more surprising, and that is the puzzle the גמרא asks about next.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come to a place
Wine
Beer

phrases.aramaic: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בִּיסְנָא אִיקְּלַע לְמַרְגְּוָאן,
phrases.english: רב שמואל בר ביסנא happened to come to מרגואן,
they brought him wine and he did not drink,
they brought him beer and he did not drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בִּיסְנָא אִיקְּלַע לְמַרְגְּוָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about how אמוראים treated גוים' beer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב שמואל בר ביסנא refused both the wine and the beer of מרגואן.

steps.title: Why did he refuse the beer?
steps.stepSummary: Refusing the wine makes sense because of a trace of עבודה זרה. But why refuse the beer?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he refused the wine, because of a trace of idol-worship. But why did he refuse the beer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the story. The wine refusal is clear, but the beer refusal needs an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is linked to idol offerings (נסך), so even a trace of that is a reason to avoid it. Beer has no such link, so the גמרא asks what his reason could be.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that, used to accept one part before asking about another
A trace or hint, here a hint of idol-worship

phrases.english: It makes sense with the wine, because of a trace,
phrases.notes: A trace of wine poured as an offering to idols.

phrases.english: but the beer, for what reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא חַמְרָא מִשּׁוּם שִׁימְצָא, שִׁיכְרָא מִשּׁוּם מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the beer refusal in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב שמואל בר ביסנא refused the beer, when beer has no direct link to idol offerings.

steps.title: A trace of a trace
steps.stepSummary: He refused the beer because of a 'trace of a trace' of עבודה זרה. Avoiding the beer kept him far from the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of a trace of a trace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he avoided the beer as a second step of distance. It kept him away from the wine, which itself was avoided because of a trace of idol-worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine is one step away from idol-worship, and the beer is one more step away. רב שמואל בר ביסנא was being extra careful and kept a double fence.

keyTerms.meaning: A trace of a trace, a double fence of distance

steps.whatToRemember: Some אמוראים went beyond the basic law. רב אחאי took the beer home, and רב שמואל בר ביסנא avoided beer as a 'trace of a trace' of עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Because of a trace of a trace.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם שִׁימְצָא דְּשִׁימְצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He avoided the beer as a second layer of distance. Beer leads to wine, and wine carries a trace of idol-worship.

steps.title: רב: Aramean beer is permitted, but his son should not drink it
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that non-Jews' beer is permitted, yet says his son חייא should not drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: This beer of the Arameans is permitted, but my son חייא should not drink from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a ruling that sounds like it contradicts itself. The beer is permitted, but his own son should stay away from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the סוגיא gave two reasons for the ban on beer of גוים: חתנות and גילוי (Step 6). Here רב calls the beer permitted but makes an exception for one person. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Beer
Aramean, meaning a non-Jew
Permitted

phrases.english: Rav said:
This beer of the Arameans is permitted,
but my son Chiyya should not drink from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הַאי שִׁיכְרָא דַּאֲרַמָּאָה שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about non-Jews' beer after the stories about drinking it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Aramean beer is permitted, but רב's son חייא should not drink it.

steps.title: Either way, רב's statement seems inconsistent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the beer is permitted it is permitted for everyone, and if forbidden it is forbidden for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if it is permitted, it is permitted for everyone. If it is forbidden, it is forbidden for everyone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. A ruling of מותר or אסור should apply to all people, so why single out his son?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack uses a two-sided argument, called מה נפשך. Neither choice explains why one person should be treated differently, so רב's two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you want it, a two-sided challenge
Forbidden
For everyone

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it?
If it is permitted, it is permitted for everyone,
if it is forbidden, it is forbidden for everyone!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ? אִי שְׁרֵי — לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of רב's ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that the beer is permitted but forbidden to his son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prohibition based on הלכה applies equally to all people, so there is no room for a personal exception.

steps.title: The concern is snake venom, which only harms a weak person
steps.stepSummary: רב's concern is גילוי. The hops weaken the venom so it is safe for most people, but not for a weak person like חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב holds the concern is exposure. The bitterness of the hops weakens the venom, but a weak person is weakened even more by it. My son חייא is weak, so he should not drink it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב holds the beer ban is about גילוי, the same reason רב נחמן gave in Step 6. Because the danger is to health, it can depend on the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is גילוי: a snake may have drunk from uncovered liquid and left venom in it. The bitter hops spoil the venom enough to make it safe for a healthy person. A danger to health can differ from person to person, so the exception for weak חייא now makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquid left uncovered, which a snake may have poisoned
Hops, a bitter plant used in beer
Venom
Weak, frail

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same גילוי reason from Step 6, not the חתנות reason. Since the worry is a danger to health, it can apply to one person and not another.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav holds that the concern is because of exposure,
phrases.notes: Uncovered liquid is worrying because a snake might have drunk from it and left venom behind.

phrases.english: and the bitterness of the hops goes
and spoils its venom,
but someone who is weak is weakened by it even more,
and my son Chiyya, since he is weak,
should not drink from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַב סָבַר מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by redefining the nature of רב's concern.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason: a health danger instead of a halachic prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's statement is about a halachic prohibition, which must apply equally to everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern is snake venom from גילוי. The hops neutralize it for healthy people but not for weak people like חייא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that rules based on danger can depend on a person's health, unlike ordinary prohibitions.

steps.title: שמואל: all creeping animals have venom, but only a snake's kills
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that every שרץ has venom, but only snake venom is deadly.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: All creeping animals have venom. A snake's venom kills; the venom of other creeping animals does not kill.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the topic of venom, the גמרא brings a related teaching from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל separates the snake from other creeping animals. All of them carry venom, but only the snake's is deadly.

keyTerms.meaning: Creeping animals
Venom
Snake
Kills

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
All creeping animals have venom;
that of a snake kills,
that of other creeping animals does not kill.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל הַשְּׁרָצִים יֵשׁ לָהֶן אֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the topic of venom raised in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All creeping animals have venom; only snake venom is deadly.

steps.title: רב's teaching on why the Arameans swell but do not die
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells חייא בר רב that his father said the Arameans swell from drinking uncovered liquids but survive because eating creeping animals heats their bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to חייא בר רב: Son of a lion, come and I will tell you a fine teaching your father רב used to say. Your father said: These Arameans are swollen because they drink exposed liquids. The reason they do not die is that they eat repulsive and creeping creatures, which heat their bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל passes on a teaching from רב to רב's son חייא. It explains why non-Jews who drink uncovered liquids survive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The venom from uncovered drinks does affect the Arameans, so they swell. But their diet of creeping creatures heats their bodies, and that protects them from dying. This fits the earlier idea that how strongly venom works depends on the person's body.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of a lion, a term of praise
A fine, excellent teaching
Swollen
Repulsive creatures and creeping animals
Heats up

steps.whatToRemember: Venom from uncovered liquid affects people differently. The hops weaken it, a weak person is more at risk, and the Arameans' diet protects them from dying even though they swell.

steps.title: רב יוסף introduces a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement from רב יוסף, which continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said:

steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the attribution appears here. The actual statement of רב יוסף follows next, so wait to see what he adds before drawing conclusions.
